subchronic exposure to dietary EPN or leptophos resulted in delayed ataxia in mallard ducks and that this was associated with inhibition of brain neurotoxic esterases and histological evidence of axonal degeneration in the spinal cord.
mallard hens were less sensitive to subchronic exposure to organophosphate insecticides that induce neuropathy than chickens and that histological changes were similar to chickens.

mallards exposed to subchronic organophosphate insecticide treatment exhibit delayed neurotoxic signs, including ataxia, paralysis, and weight loss, as well as inhibition of neurotoxic esterases and histological lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurotoxic potential of organophosphorus compounds.
the neurotoxicity of organophosphorus compounds in birds, and the effects on birds of exposure to the organophosphate insecticide, leptophos.
the effects of organophosphorus pesticides on the nervous system of the mallard.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EPN and leptophos are neurotoxicants for mallard ducks and that the mallard is probably a more sensitive species than chickens to the delayed effects of these organophosphorus compounds.

mallards are somewhat less sensitive than adult chickens to the delayed neurotoxic effects of organophosphorus pesticides, but that they are still very susceptible to these effects.

the mallard is a more sensitive indicator of subacute and subchronic organophosphate neurotoxicity than the bobwhite.
the mallard is a sensitive species for the induction of delayed neurotoxic symptoms, and that the mallard brain is sensitive for the inhibition of neurotoxic esterases.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we have a good understanding of the mechanisms of organophosphorus-induced delayed neurotoxiciy (OPIDN) and that it can be induced by a variety of OP compounds that share a common mechanism of action.
birds are more sensitive to OPIDN than mammals and that the mallard duck is a good model for OPIDN.
